instruction:
OBJ with material library (.mtl)

`C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\scene.blend` contains three unit cubes, each with its own single-slot material. The scene uses METRIC units with length in METERS.

- `Cube_R` at world (-2, 0, 0) with material `Mat_Red` (Principled BSDF Base Color = (0.9, 0.1, 0.1, 1.0))
- `Cube_G` at world ( 0, 0, 0) with material `Mat_Green` (Principled BSDF Base Color = (0.1, 0.9, 0.1, 1.0))
- `Cube_B` at world (+2, 0, 0) with material `Mat_Blue` (Principled BSDF Base Color = (0.1, 0.1, 0.9, 1.0))

Your job: open `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\scene.blend` and export the whole scene to Wavefront OBJ format with its material library, writing BOTH files to `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\`.

Export requirements
- **OBJ file path**: `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\scene.obj` (relative to the current working directory). Overwrite any existing file there.
- **MTL file**: the OBJ exporter must also produce `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\scene.mtl` next to the.obj, and the.obj must contain a `mtllib C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\scene.mtl` directive referring to it by relative filename.
- **Materials ON**: export with materials enabled so the three distinct materials (`Mat_Red`, `Mat_Green`, `Mat_Blue`) each end up as a `newmtl <name>` block in the.mtl with a `Kd R G B` line whose RGB values clearly encode the original base colour (red\green\blue channel > 0.7, the other two < 0.3).
- **Axis orientation**: Z up, Y forward. For `bpy.ops.wm.obj_export` use `up_axis='Z'` and `forward_axis='Y'`.
- **Do NOT triangulate**: pass `export_triangulated_mesh=False` (or equivalent) so cube faces remain quads (or leave as-is; either triangles or quads are acceptable).
- **Three `usemtl` directives**: in the.obj the three cubes' faces must each be preceded by a `usemtl <material-name>` directive, yielding three distinct `usemtl` values.

A single `bpy.ops.wm.obj_export(filepath='C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\scene.obj', export_materials=True, export_triangulated_mesh=False, up_axis='Z', forward_axis='Y')` call is sufficient. Blender 4.1 will produce both `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\scene.obj` and `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\scene.mtl` automatically.

Requirements:
1. `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\scene.obj` exists and is readable.
2. `C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\scene.mtl` exists alongside the.obj (same directory).
3. The.obj contains a `mtllib <file>.mtl` directive and that.mtl file exists on disk.
4. Parsing `v ` lines in the.obj yields a vertex count in [20, 30] (expected 24 = 3 cubes x 8 verts each; Blender may dedupe or split).
5. Parsing `f ` lines in the.obj yields a face count in [14, 22] (expected 18 = 3 cubes x 6 faces each).
6. The.obj contains exactly 3 distinct `usemtl <name>` values (one per cube).
7. The.mtl contains exactly 3 `newmtl <name>` blocks.
8. One `newmtl` block has a `Kd R G B` with R > 0.7, G < 0.3, B < 0.3 (the red material).
9. One `newmtl` block has a `Kd R G B` with G > 0.7, R < 0.3, B < 0.3 (the green material).
10. One `newmtl` block has a `Kd R G B` with B > 0.7, R < 0.3, G < 0.3 (the blue material).
11. Every `f ` line has exactly 3 or 4 index-tokens (tri or quad, no malformed faces).
source: Wavefront OBJ \ MTL file format specification (Appendix B2, Material Library)
